subject.title: Feature Request: Add .gitignore-like exclude patterns to backup CLI

question: Should OpenClaw core add a native user-controlled backup exclude surface now, and if so should it use the linked PR’s full `--exclude`/`--exclude-file`/smart-default/protected-path contract or a narrower safe-default design?
rationale: This is not a strict bug fix: it adds public CLI flags and changes the backup security/restorability contract, while current discussion includes both native implementation attempts and a ClawHub workaround.

options.title: Review native exclude support
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 or a replacement as the implementation path after conflict, proof, protected-path, and security review are resolved.

options.title: Narrow to curated skips
options.body: Keep core focused on safe built-in omissions like volatile state and rebuildable dependencies, and defer arbitrary user patterns until a smaller contract is proposed.

options.title: Defer to ClawHub backup tooling
options.body: Leave native backup unchanged for now and point users to external backup plugins such as Keep My Claw for focused backup policy.

recommendation.title: Review native exclude support
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 or a replacement as the implementation path after conflict, proof, protected-path, and security review are resolved.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged and reviewed the original backup CLI feature, so they are the strongest history-backed owner for the native backup contract decision.
